summary: Slice A1 of 0.8.7, the sealed room, built in the worktree (not committed). New workbench/brain_seal.py holds the walls: a closed allow-list lint of the runtime's launch line (100 forbidden names from the b11669 help in 10 reasons, agent tools with their shell first; --name=value and _ spellings caught; --offline required), the environment allow-list (PATH, locale, the runtime's own library folder; for Vulkan XDG_RUNTIME_DIR and a shader cache under Graphite's state), the private socket (m.sock in the start's 0700 folder or a short 0700 folder; loopback only where no socket can be had), HTTP over AF_UNIX, and the seal check run in local_brain._start_server every time a model starts, before Ready and before the model is asked anything: /tools 403, /slots and POST /props 501, chat without her key and with a random second key 401, /proc/<runtime>/environ only allowed names, its network namespace its own, no internet socket out or bound. A failure refuses Ready with her one line ("I didn't start the model: it accepted a key I didn't make. Nothing was asked of it.") and never triggers the Vulkan-to-CPU retry. brain_worker._child_setup unshares a user and a network namespace before exec; where the computer refuses it writes GRAPHITE_NETWORK_NOT_SEALED to the runtime log, the model still starts offline and the seal record says NETWORK_NOT_SEALED with the reason, shown in words ("Not sealed from the network on this computer; started offline."). brain_runtime.worker_environment is replaced by the allow-list; device discovery looks from inside the sealed room first, and when the Radeon is seen only outside it the model starts on the Radeon unsealed and labelled, with "Use the processor, sealed" one press away in the Brain room (open question 4's default). slate_stream streams over the socket; the Brain room shows the seal line, a 'How I know' fold and her refusal line; brain.status carries the seal and its words; the qualification receipt carries the seal's state and digest for A5's key. New workbench/seal_model_checks.py is the real-runtime seal check beside joined_model_checks.py. One real start of the 4B here (CPU, under the model lock) passed every wall, sealed, with canary LLAMA_API_KEY and HF_TOKEN in Graphite's own environment refused and absent. Nothing was tested in the owner's sense and nothing ran on the ThinkPad.
files_changed: tools/campaign_lib/sim.py (simulation harness: answers the new seal_check seam)
tools/check_hatch.py (one ON_DEMAND_CHECKS line for the new model check)
smoke: Script b087/A1/smoke.py on a throwaway copy (output b087/A1/smoke.out); stand-in runtimes are b087/A1/standin.py, a computer that refuses namespaces is b087/A1/refuse_wrapper.py (os.unshare raising EPERM in the supervisor).

Forbidden arguments from the b11669 help: 'A1 help options: 417 | forbidden names: 100 | forbidden not in help: [] | allowed not in help: []' and 'A2 forbidden vectors (name, name=value, name_with_underscores): 282 refused; by reason {AGENT_TOOLS: 23, KEY_ON_COMMAND_LINE: 3, ENDPOINTS: 51, DOWNLOADS: 83, OTHER_MODELS: 52, NETWORK: 24, READS_FILES: 13, WRITES_TO_DISK: 14, VERBOSE_LOGS: 16, RUNS_PROGRAMS: 3} | not refused or wrong reason: []'.

Every other help option off the allow-list: 'A3 ... 293 refused as not on my list; passed through: []'. Graphite's own line passes: 'A0 ... 37 arguments'. '--tools all' -> "I didn't start the model: its launch line holds --tools, and it would turn on agent tools, a shell among them. Nothing was asked of it."; no --offline -> "... its launch line lacks --offline ..."; --api-key -> "... it would put a key on the command line, where other programs can read it ..."; --host 0.0.0.0, a URL model, --port beside a socket and a repeated --threads all refused.

Environment with LLAMA_API_KEY, HF_TOKEN, GGML_BACKEND_PATH, LLAMA_CACHE, HTTPS_PROXY, LD_PRELOAD, LLAMA_ARG_TOOLS, LLAMA_BATCH_DEBUG set in Graphite's own environment: 'B1 CPU environment names: [LANG, LC_CTYPE, LD_LIBRARY_PATH, PATH]', 'B2 VULKAN ...: [LANG, LC_CTYPE, LD_LIBRARY_PATH, MESA_SHADER_CACHE_DIR, PATH, XDG_RUNTIME_DIR]'.

Good stand-in through the real local_brain._start_server: 'C1 ... READY | seal SEALED | transport PRIVATE_SOCKET | its env [LANG, LC_CTYPE, LD_LIBRARY_PATH, PATH] | own network True | --offline True | socket m.sock | umask 0o77' and 'C1 LLAMA_API_KEY or HF_TOKEN in the runtime environ: []'; words 'Sealed: it can only answer. No tools, no network, only the key I made, and only Graphite can reach it.'; completion, health and slate_stream over the socket gave 'ready'; a stream with a wrong key gave LOCAL_STREAM_HTTP_401.

Stand-in that connects to 1.1.1.1:443, sealed: 'C3 ... tcp [101, OSError] udp [101, OSError] (ENETUNREACH is 101) | REFUSED: ... it opened a network socket of its own beside its private socket ...' (the failed UDP attempt leaves a bound port, which the check refuses).
Stand-in answering /tools with 200: 'C4 ... I didn't start the model: it offers built-in tools. Nothing was asked of it.'
Stand-in accepting a second key: 'C5 ... I didn't start the model: it accepted a key I didn't make. Nothing was asked of it.'
Namespaces refused, outward stand-in: 'C6 ... tcp CONNECTED udp CONNECTED | MODEL_SEAL_REFUSED: I didn't start the model: it reached out to the network. Nothing was asked of it.'

Namespaces refused, good stand-in: 'C7 ... READY | seal NETWORK_NOT_SEALED | reason COMPUTER_REFUSED: EPERM | own network False | --offline True' and 'C7 words: Not sealed from the network on this computer; started offline. | sealed processor offered: False'.

Open question 4: 'D1 device discovery, sealed first: AVAILABLE | network_seal VULKAN_NOT_SEEN_IN_ITS_OWN_NETWORK', 'D2 start_server then asks for the network seal: False', 'D3 ... button: Use the processor, sealed'; the Brain room's seal row on offscreen widgets showed the line, 'How I know' and the button, and hid all three with no model.

Real runtime, one start of the 4B (CPU, b11669 from the pinned archive, under the model lock, 09:31:57 to 09:32:25 UTC): python -m workbench.seal_model_checks printed state PASSED, seal SEALED, transport PRIVATE_SOCKET, activation 14.6 s; walls: inherited LLAMA_API_KEY 401, her key 200 ('ready' in 1.24 s), /tools 403, /slots 501, POST /props 501, no key 401, second key 401, environ [LC_CTYPE, LD_LIBRARY_PATH, PATH], network its own, internet sockets 0. The runtime log said 'listening on unix:///tmp/graphite-<8>/m.sock' (the scratch path was too long for the start folder, so the short folder was used and was removed at stop).
existing_tests_changed: No file under tests_integrated was changed, deleted or skipped.

tools/campaign_lib/sim.py (the simulation harness behind tests_integrated/test_resource_rules.py and the R campaign cases) now also patches local_brain.seal_check with a sealed record marked simulated: a scripted worker has no process, socket or environ for the real check to read, so without it every simulated start would be refused. No expectation changed; not run (the owner's rule).
sockets: None used: A1 is engine-only (lane A) and plugs into no 0.8.6 socket (reading.py, the OpenPoint, answer_check, phrases, mind_words). None missing for this slice.
Merge note: her column (0.8.6 mind_panel_qt.py) does not show the seal line; brain.status carries 'seal' and 'seal_words' for it to place at merge if wanted.
decisions: Open question 4's fallback is decided by device discovery, not by a second model load: the --list-devices probe runs inside the sealed room first (through brain_worker, as a model would run); only if the Radeon is seen outside but not inside does the model start on Vulkan without its own network (labelled, reason VULKAN_NOT_SEEN_IN_ITS_OWN_NETWORK, the sealed processor one press away). Reason: no extra load attempts on the 35B, and the existing Vulkan-to-CPU retry and its campaign expectations (backends tried [VULKAN, CPU]) stay as they are.
A seal refusal (MODEL_SEAL_REFUSED) never triggers the Vulkan-to-CPU retry: a refusal stands and she says why.
Where the computer refuses namespaces altogether the label is the same words, and the sealed processor is not offered (it would not be sealed either).

The socket goes in the start's own 0700 folder when the path fits 107 bytes, else in a short 0700 mkdtemp folder under XDG_RUNTIME_DIR or the temporary folder (removed at stop); loopback only where no AF_UNIX socket can be had (Windows); the network seal is applied only behind a socket, since loopback inside an empty network cannot be reached.

No uid map is written in the new user namespace: the runtime runs as the overflow user with no capability outside it; file access is unchanged. The unshare comes before the limits and the parent-death signal in _child_setup, and the runtime gets a 077 umask.

The lint is closed: anything not on the allow-list is refused; the 100 named ones get their reason. Verbose-log and log-file options are forbidden (they could carry prompt text), and an option given twice is refused. --checkpoint-min-step is pre-admitted for A2's launch line (design 4.2); nothing else of A2's is.

The seal check refuses any internet socket the runtime holds that is connected outward or bound to a port (the pinned runtime behind its socket holds none, measured here and by the trust lens); this also catches the bound port a failed outward UDP attempt leaves inside the empty network.

Her sealed line says 'only the key I made' instead of the trust lens's 'none of your files': the runtime still runs as the owner's user and could read files if it had tools, so that claim would overreach.

The seal digest covers every check's outcome, the environment's names, the launch line's shape and the runtime pin, never a path, key or process number; it is kept in the worker record and in the qualification receipt (receipt.seal) for A5's qualification key.
The seal check is a seam of its own (local_brain.seal_check) so the campaign simulation can answer it; a real start always runs brain_seal.check.
continuing_work.executor_identity now digests brain_seal.py with the other executor files, so a change to the seal changes the executor identity.
No kernel operation, job tool or setting was added, so the registry record was not regenerated.
not_done: Vulkan inside the sealed room was not tried (no GPU here); the ThinkPad's first evening should run python -m workbench.seal_model_checks --backend VULKAN (A5's kit can call it).

worker_boundary's protected MODEL profile (worker_tasks.model_task) was not changed: it already runs inside its own boundary with a private network, but its launch line is not linted and has no --offline.
Windows: the loopback fallback, the environment allow-list's Windows names and os.execve were not run anywhere.
The qualification key itself is A5's; only the seal digest is provided.
Her column (0.8.6) shows no seal line; the Brain room and brain.status do.

No test files were written; the test suite, the tiers, the window checks and the R campaign were not run (the owner's rule), including tests_integrated/test_resource_rules.py, which runs through the changed sim.py.
Nothing ran on the owner's ThinkPad.
release_note: Kas's model now runs in a sealed room: it gets only the settings she allows (a key your shell sets for another tool, such as LLAMA_API_KEY or HF_TOKEN, no longer reaches it), listens on a private socket only she can reach, starts offline with no agent tools, and runs in its own empty network where the computer allows it. Each time the model starts she checks the seal before it is ready, and if a check fails she does not start it and says why in one line. Where the computer refuses the network seal, or the Radeon cannot be seen inside it, she says 'Not sealed from the network on this computer; started offline', and the sealed processor is one press away in the Brain room. This was not tested before release (we test before 0.8.8); one start of the 4B on the build machine passed the seal check, and the seal has not been tried with Vulkan or on the ThinkPad.
